name: Mk.gee
label: R&R
lede: Michael Gordon grew up in Linwood, New Jersey, recording on cracked software and cheap gear, then spent years putting his guitar on other people's records. In 2024 his own debut, Two Star & the Dream Police, runs 33 minutes and gets argued over everywhere.

eras.title: A Linwood kid and a Portastudio
eras.text: Gordon records every instrument himself, leaves USC, and by 2019 has a single, two EPs and deals with IAMSOUND and Interscope. The gear is cheap and the guitar is played like a synth.

years.h: Linwood to USC and back out
years.p: Michael Gordon grows up in Linwood, New Jersey, graduates from Mainland Regional High School in 2015, and leaves USC's Thornton School of Music a year later.
years.xp:
PhillyVoice has him starting piano and composition at age 5, with grandparents who ran a jazz society in nearby Somers Point. He told the paper that making music wasn't cool in Linwood, and that he'd formed a band with classmates years earlier.

Dazed has him growing up on cracked Ableton and still favoring what he calls cheap, bad gear, because it forces him to solve problems. Sources disagree on his birth year: Wikipedia says 1996, Dazed says 1997.

years.h: "I Know How You Get" arrives under a name people have to be taught
years.p: Gordon puts out his first single as Mk.gee, pronounced McGee.
Orchard Ears releases the home-recorded EP, with "Roll with the Punches" and "Over Here" among the songs.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists "Roll with the Punches", "Over Here" and "You" as the singles. PhillyVoice says Frank Ocean's Blonded Radio played the EP, which is how a lot of listeners first heard of him.

years.p: A second EP on Orchard Ears, led by "Come On (You Know That I'm a Fool)" and "New Year".
play: Come On (You Know That I'm a Fool)

years.cap: Mk.gee opening for Wallows at Wonder Ballroom, Portland, April 22, 2019
years.h: A double signing, then a year opening for other people
years.p: Gordon signs with IAMSOUND and Interscope, opens for Omar Apollo and Wallows, and plays Pitchfork Music Festival Paris, his first festival.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts him on Apollo's Voyager Tour and Wallows' Nothing Happens Tour in 2019. The single "Untitled" is the first release under the new deal.

eras.title: The guitar behind other people's names
eras.text: His own releases thin out while his fingerprints show up on Omar Apollo's and Dijon's records and on a Charlotte Day Wilson song that Drake and Travis Scott end up sampling. The partnership with Dijon starts here.

years.h: A Museum of Contradiction, in under 25 minutes
years.p: The Interscope mixtape runs on bedroom funk and psychedelia, follows the February single "cz", and gets four stars from NME.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it at 24 minutes 45 seconds, on IAMSOUND and Interscope, with Andrew Sarlo engineering and mixing and Joseph Thornalley co-producing ">;0" with Vegyn. NME's Rhys Buchanan called it a release that "merges genres from different worlds with both maturity and ease".

years.cap: Dijon (left) and Mk.gee onstage on Bon Iver's 2022 tour
years.h: Dijon's Absolutely, and a sample Drake and Travis Scott use
years.p: Mk.gee co-produces [[Dijon|cceea21d-f3ec-4586-be7a-d2e939c15c78]]'s debut album and co-writes "Mountains" with Charlotte Day Wilson, which Drake and Travis Scott later sample on "Fair Trade".
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls Absolutely (November 2021) self-produced by Dijon "alongside frequent collaborator Mk.gee". The Dijon and Mk.gee partnership runs through everything that follows, including Two Star.

Wikipedia also credits Gordon with co-producing Omar Apollo's 2020 mixtape Apolonio.

eras.title: Two Star, one Portastudio
eras.text: After four years without a release of his own, Gordon puts out a debut album that critics keep describing and can't quite place. It makes him one of the year's most discussed guitarists.

years.p: The first preview of the album is a funk-leaning, lo-fi double single. Rolling Stone's Joshua Minsoo Kim later calls "How Many Miles" the album's highlight.

years.src: Wikipedia: Two Star & the Dream Police
yt: Are You Looking Up, Jimmy Kimmel Live (April 2024)
years.h: Dazed and The Fader rank the singles before the album exists
years.p: Dazed puts "Are You Looking Up" at No. 12 of 2023 and The Fader puts "You Got It" at No. 26, off a double single released October 20.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes "You Got It" later shows up in the third season of The Bear. A five-date "Inside Each of Us Are Two Stars" tour had opened at Music Hall of Williamsburg in Brooklyn on October 16.

"Are You Looking Up" also became his first network TV performance, on Jimmy Kimmel Live! in April 2024.

years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Two Star & the Dream Police · Dazed · Rolling Stone
years.h: Two Star & the Dream Police lands to a 7.8 from Pitchfork
years.p: Twelve songs in 33 minutes, mixed by Gordon himself and co-produced with [[Dijon|cceea21d-f3ec-4586-be7a-d2e939c15c78]], on R&R.
years.xp:
The Pitchfork score is 78 on Album of the Year's critic list (review by Brady Brickner-Wood), who called it a "magnificent debut album". Metacritic shows 83 from four reviews. Anthony Fantano's Needle Drop gave it 60, the low score in that list, while the Guardian and the Arts Desk gave 100.

Dazed says Andrew Sarlo helped with arranging and Gordon played everything else. Rolling Stone points to how he uses silence: on "New Low" he "doesn't utter a word during the final 30 seconds".

Mastering is split between Heba Kadry ("How Many Miles", "Candy") and Simon Lancelot. Wikipedia lists the label as R&R.

years.src: Wikipedia: Two Star & the Dream Police · Year-End Lists
years.h: Clash, Dazed and the New York Times put it first for 2024
years.p: Jon Caramanica's New York Times list agrees; the New Yorker and Gorilla vs. Bear go second, and Pitchfork's own list has it 18th.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's reception section also lists it No. 3 at the Los Angeles Times, No. 7 at the Line of Best Fit, and top 20 at NME, the Guardian and Rolling Stone. In October 2024 Pitchfork put it No. 91 on its 100 Best Albums of the 2020s So Far, less than five years into the decade.

"Alesis" was the most-listed single, No. 1 of the year at Coup De Main and Vulture.

q: He has found things to do on the guitar that are like nobody else.
years.h: Eric Clapton names Mk.gee when asked who excites him on guitar
years.p: Eric Clapton compares Michael Gordon's arrival to Prince's. Gordon plays a Fender Jaguar strung as a baritone, through a Roland guitar-synth pickup and a Portastudio 424 used as a preamp.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Clapton called Gordon unique and said he can "do it live" too. The rig, also per Wikipedia: flatwound strings on the Jaguar, a Roland GK-2A divided pickup into a VG-8, and the Portastudio's cassette-style clipping left in on purpose.

years.cap: Mk.gee at Electric Brixton, London, October 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: Two Star & the Dream Police
yt: Alesis, live at the Fonda, Los Angeles
years.h: The world tour runs September 2 to December 7, Vancouver to Melbourne
years.p: It follows 18 North American dates in April and May. Live clips, like "Alesis" at the Fonda in Los Angeles, become events of their own.
years.xp:
Billboard wrote that his Los Angeles show proved "good music alone can carry a great show". The Guardian described a room of newfound obsessives with arena rock energy, and NME called London an almost religious experience.

Wikipedia tracks these from the tour dates and the review round-ups cited in the album article.

years.p: Gordon plays "Alesis" and the standalone single "Rockman", out October 18, which becomes his first charting single.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Gordon co-wrote "Rockman" with Zack Sekoff, who plays in his live band, and produced it himself. It peaked at No. 24 on Adult Alternative Airplay, No. 25 on Alternative Airplay and No. 30 on Rock & Alternative Airplay. It was nominated for Record of the Year at the 2025 Libera Awards.

His first TV performance had been Jimmy Kimmel Live! in April, with "Are You Looking Up".

eras.title: The sound on everyone's record
eras.text: What Two Star made recognizable carries into pop's biggest rooms, with Gordon credited on records by Justin Bieber and Bon Iver while he keeps playing festivals under his own name.

years.big: "Anything that comes out of his mouth is pop music."
q: You can really do pretty wild stuff behind that.
years.h: Justin Bieber's "Daisies" reaches No. 2 with Mk.gee in the credits
years.p: Gordon, asked about writing for Bieber, co-produces and co-writes the lead single from Swag with Dijon, among others. It peaks at No. 2 on the Hot 100 and is Grammy-nominated.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Dijon, Mk.gee, Eddie Benjamin, Carter Lang, Dylan Wiggins and Daniel Chetrit as producers, with Tobias Jesso Jr. as a songwriter. Tonitruale reports Mk.gee receives official credit on "Daisies" while his guitar sound runs through the album. Gordon also co-wrote "Love Song" on Swag II.

years.h: Gordon co-writes Bon Iver's "From", then plays festivals on two continents
years.p: He, Justin Vernon and Tobias Jesso Jr. write "From" for Sable, Fable; his own sets include Governors Ball, Lollapalooza, Øya and Austin City Limits.
years.xp: Wikipedia also lists him on the BBC's Sound of 2025 nominees and Libera Awards nominations for Best Breakthrough Artist and Record of the Year. Dijon, his main partner, released his second album Baby on August 15, 2025, and appears on Bon Iver's "Day One".
